characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. assamica, primarily plantation bushes
characteristics.oxidation: Full accelerated post-fermentation via the wet-piling process (wo dui)
characteristics.harvestSeason: Summer and autumn harvests are commonly used for shou pu-erh
characteristics.teaware: Clay teapot (Yixing clay softens the flavor nicely)

description.short: Dark tea with accelerated fermentation, smooth and earthy, ready to enjoy immediately after production
description.overview: Menghai is the heartland of shou pu-erh production, where the wet-piling (wo dui) technique was refined in 1973, producing the taste of aged tea in just several weeks instead of decades.
description.leaf: Dark-brown to nearly black leaves, loose or compressed into cakes, tuocha, or bricks
description.liquor: Deep dark-red to nearly black, thick and opaque liquor
description.aroma: Earthy, nutty, with nuances of wet wood, forest floor, or dried prunes
description.taste: Mellow, thick, without astringency or bitterness, offering nutty depth and gentle sweetness
description.processing: Plucking → withering → fixation → rolling → drying (maocha) → wet-piling fermentation (wo dui) in piles for 40–60 days with periodic turning and temperature control → drying → optional steam compression

history.origin: Prior to 1973, all pu-erh was produced using only the "raw" (sheng) method and required years of natural aging to soften
history.development: The wo dui technique was developed by teams at the Kunming and Menghai tea factories to satisfy surging demand—especially from Hong Kong—for mellow aged flavor without the long wait
history.modern: Today, Menghai Tea Factory (founded in 1940) remains the benchmark producer of shou pu-erh, and classic recipes like "7572" set the standard for the entire industry
interestingFacts: The recipe code "7572" signifies the year the recipe was created (1975), the leaf grade (7), and the factory code (2 for Menghai)
Shou pu-erh is frequently recommended to newcomers as an approachable and gentle entry into the world of dark fermented teas
